q: How should an electronics plant report fluorinated gases used in etching and chamber cleaning?
title: Electronics plants: fluorinated gases
short: Count what is not destroyed. Gases such as CF4, C2F6, NF3 and SF6 are used in etch and clean steps; part reacts, part is broken down in abatement, and the rest escapes. IPCC 2006 gives default use and destruction rates, but purchase records and abatement data per tool give a far better figure.
audience: Wafer fabs, display makers and back end plants in Penang, Kulim, Singapore and India's new semiconductor parks

ul: Gas bought and drawn per tool, from purchase and cylinder records.
Share used up in the process, from the tool or IPCC defaults.
Share destroyed by point of use abatement, from tested efficiency.
Remaining emissions x the gas's GWP.

p: These gases have global warming potentials thousands to tens of thousands of times CO2, so small leaks can rival a plant's electricity emissions.

ul: Nitrous oxide used in some deposition steps.
By products formed in the process, such as CF4 from other gases.

senseible: Senseible reads gas, refrigerant and electricity invoices into a dated, fingerprinted record, so the quantities behind each gas figure trace back to the documents.
